plotTitle: The Ancients Lab: Descent into Mutation
mainObjective: Investigate the arcane disturbances and spreading corruption emanating from the long-lost dwarven research facility buried beneath Blackcrag, traverse the tainted wilderness and forsaken vaults, and confront the mutated horrors and rogue constructs within before the land is consumed. But know this: the Thing below has been called sleeper and warden, ancestor and invitation, reflection and abyss. The facility has shown many faces to many visitors, and the truth you find may depend on which questions you dare to ask. Every choice resonates with the presence below, tilting the balance toward dreams, containment, communion, inheritance, or mirrors.

plotPoints.title: The Marches Beckon
plotPoints.description: The party arrives at the Blackcrag Marches (BA001), drawn by rumors of strange lights and ancient machinery stirring beneath the hills. Locals speak of arcane disturbances and missing livestock, all pointing toward a hidden dwarven facility. To proceed, the party must investigate the surface mysteries and seek clues about the sealed laboratory's location.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Introduces the main quest and hooks the party into exploring the Marches. Sets tone and context.

sideQuests.title: Echoes in the Heather
sideQuests.description: A local shepherd asks for help finding missing sheep—lost to the mists, or perhaps something stranger. Tracking the sheep to a collapsed vent, the party finds hints of ancient machinery and mutated wildlife.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Reveals evidence of the hidden structure and foreshadows later dangers.

sideQuests.title: Whispering Stones
sideQuests.description: Standing stones atop a windswept ridge bear cryptic runes that shift when read by different observers. A dream-sensitive reader sees sleep-wards meant to soothe; a containment-focused reader sees seal-marks reinforcing a prison; a communion-seeker sees invitation-text calling the willing; a genealogist sees ancestral glyphs naming the buried lineage; a fearful reader sees warning-script about what the mirror reflects. Deciphering them grants lore about the facility builders and warns of the Thing awakening below--but which truth the runes reveal depends on who reads them.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Provides foreshadowing and possible clues to bypass later traps.

plotPoints.title: Descent into the Forsaken Galleries
plotPoints.description: Clues from the Marches lead the party to a hidden entrance among the basalt outcrops. They descend into the Abandoned Vaultways (FG001), a dwarven tunnel complex now infested with scavengers warped by ancient technology. Here, they must navigate hazardous corridors and seek out the Rambling Dwarven Survivor, whose knowledge is vital for entering the deeper laboratory.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Transitions the party from surface exploration to dungeon crawl. Introduces mutated scavengers and environmental hazards.

sideQuests.title: The Archivist's Map
sideQuests.description: A forgotten scholar in Ostmere claims to have fragments of an ancient map that shows hidden entrances and traps within the Vaultways. Convincing or helping the scholar could grant the party valuable intel or shortcuts.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Provides the party with a partial map or clues to avoid deadly traps, impacting later exploration and encounter options.

sideQuests.title: Lost Offerings
sideQuests.description: Residents of Grimhollow Outskirts beg the party to retrieve tokens left at the vault's old shrine, said to placate vengeful spirits. They offer a protective charm in return.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Party gains a charm that may help with social encounters or provide advantage on saves versus hauntings inside the Vaultways.

sideQuests.title: A Survivor’s Tale
sideQuests.description: A rambling dwarven survivor hides among the shadows. If aided, he can share secrets of the lower levels and offer a crude map.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Provides shortcuts or warnings about traps deeper in the complex.

plotPoints.title: The Shadowed Halls
plotPoints.description: Navigating the winding, dust-choked corridors of the Vaultways, the party encounters faded murals hinting at the facility's purpose and calamity. They must contend with environmental hazards and hostile scavengers, while seeking clues about the contamination spreading into the wilds above. The survivor's information points toward deeper anomalies linked to the ancient lab below.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Builds tension through exploration and initial threats, offers the first real choices regarding approach (stealth, negotiation, or combat).

sideQuests.title: Murals of Warning
sideQuests.description: Investigating the murals reveals cryptic warnings and perhaps a hidden switch or puzzle. The murals depict different histories depending on the viewer's inclination: a dreaming god's slumber, a warden's eternal vigil, a communion ritual in progress, a genealogical record of those who became the facility, or a hall of mirrors reflecting every observer who ever stood here. Deciphering the images could disarm a deadly trap or reveal a secret passage.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Unlocks a shortcut to deeper vault sections or disables a major trap, making progress easier and safer.

sideQuests.title: A Scavenger’s Plea
sideQuests.description: A wounded scavenger, separated from their group, offers information about the dangers ahead in exchange for healing or safe passage.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Provides party with advance warning about monster lairs or rival factions, may create future allies or rivals.

plotPoints.title: The Vaults' Secret Heart
plotPoints.description: Deeper within the Vaultways, the party discovers the containment chamber--its arcane wards flickering. Inside is a living mass of shadow and memory, once a guardian, now corrupted by the same forces infecting the land. The party must decide whether to reinforce the wards, attempt to communicate, or destroy the entity before it can escape and worsen the corruption spreading toward the surface. Each choice tilts toward a different truth: reinforcing may soothe a dreaming mind or strengthen a warden's failing vigil; communicating may open communion or awaken ancestral memory; destroying may shatter a mirror or kill the last guardian of an ancient seal. The entity itself seems to invite all three responses simultaneously.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Confronts players with a moral and strategic choice that echoes across all five playlines. Reinforcing wards soothes the Dreamer but also strengthens Containment; communicating opens Communion but may unlock Inheritance; destroying risks shattering the Mirror but may be the only way to prevent the Dreamer from waking. The entity's response varies by playline: it may thank the party for lullaby, curse them for imprisonment, embrace them as kin, recognize them as descendants, or show them their own reflections dying.

sideQuests.title: Fragments of Memory
sideQuests.description: Scattered memory-stones around the containment chamber reveal more about the entity's original purpose and downfall. Each stone shows a different version of the truth: the entity as dream-warden, containment-guardian, communion-vessel, ancestral-remnant, or mirror-surface. Piecing them together may reveal that all versions are simultaneously true--or that the stones themselves reshape memory to match the reader's expectations.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Unlocks a non-violent resolution, or provides boons for the final encounter if completed.

plotPoints.title: The Gauntlet of Echoes
plotPoints.description: After resolving the situation in the Vaults' heart, the labyrinth reacts—construct defenses awaken, the halls twist, and spectral echoes attempt to bar the party's escape. The nature of these threats is shaped by the party's choices in the containment chamber, and whether the corruption is contained or unleashed. Emerging to the surface, the party finds the surrounding wilderness increasingly tainted.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Serves as the Vaultways’ climax and transition to the corrupted wilderness; party must survive and escape with whatever consequences they’ve unleashed or averted.

sideQuests.title: Echoes of Regret
sideQuests.description: Ghostly figures relive their final moments, and interacting with them may offer the party a means to calm the restless dead or gain their blessing.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Success can confer a boon for the escape or a haunting curse if mishandled.

plotPoints.title: Into the Aberrant Wastes
plotPoints.description: The party journeys into the Aberrant Wastes (AC001), a region warped by strange energies emanating from the laboratory deep below. As mutated life and environmental hazards worsen, the party must survive the hazardous landscape and seek allies—or at least the tolerance—of the twisted denizens. Clues from the Vaultways now point directly toward the heart of the corruption.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Establishes the tone and danger of the Wastes, introduces hostile and neutral factions, and sets up the mystery of the corruption’s source.

sideQuests.title: Whispers in the Wind
sideQuests.description: Strange psychic whispers lead the party to a hidden grove where a sentient fungus colony pleads for aid in resisting further mutation.
sideQuests.plotImpact: If aided, the fungus provides guidance and shortcuts through the terrain.

sideQuests.title: Scavenger’s Bargain
sideQuests.description: A desperate scavenger offers information about the core in exchange for rare, untainted supplies.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Secures a map of safe trails and warning about mutated patrols.

plotPoints.title: Shattered Realities
plotPoints.description: As the party presses deeper into the Wastes, they encounter zones where reality is thin--gravity warps, time loops, and monstrous wildlife stalks them. These thin places are the dream-surface of a sleeper, the membrane of a containment seal, the threshold of communion, the field of ancestral reversion, or the projection of collective fear. The party must choose whether to stabilize a reality rift or exploit its chaos. A hidden third option exists: step through the thinnest point and see what lies on the other side of reality itself.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Stabilizing the rift soothes the Dreamer or reinforces Containment. Exploiting chaos accelerates Communion or triggers reversion. Stepping through reveals the Mirror truth: the party sees themselves as the thin place perceives them. Each choice reshapes the landscape ahead according to which playline dominates.

sideQuests.title: Echoes of the Past
sideQuests.description: Fragments of memory linger in a time-warped zone--players can interact with them to learn about the origins of the Wastes. The memories show the facility's last moments: researchers soothing a dreamer, wardens sealing a containment breach, communion-seekers opening themselves to the presence, genealogists discovering the ancestral truth, or a mirror-room where every experiment saw only itself. Each memory fragment tilts the observer's perception of what happened here.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Provides lore and possibly reveals a weakness of the final threat.

sideQuests.title: The Reality Anchor
sideQuests.description: A malfunctioning reality anchor device can be repaired or destroyed. Repairing it stabilizes a portion of the Wastes, making travel safer but attracting hostile attention. The anchor itself serves different functions per playline: it regulates the dreamer's breath, reinforces containment geometry, maintains the communion threshold, preserves ancestral resonance, or keeps the mirror from distorting. Destroying it may free or destabilize whichever truth it serves.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Changes the landscape and affects possible reinforcements in the climax.

plotPoints.title: The Aberrant Conclave
plotPoints.description: At the center of the Wastes stands the ruined conclave, where mutated leaders and aberrant entities gather in two factions. One faction seeks to preserve the current state--the sleepers who wish to keep dreaming, the wardens who maintain containment, the gradualists who prefer slow communion, the separators who resist reversion, the reflectors who study fear. The other faction demands change--the wakers who would rouse the Dreamer, the breach-ers who would break containment, the immediatists who crave full communion now, the reverters who embrace ancestral transformation, the weaponizers who would turn fear itself into a blade. The party must ally with one faction or expose both.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Allying with preservers steers toward Dreamer-soothing or Containment-reinforcement endings. Allying with changers tilts toward Communion-completion or Inheritance-reversion. Exposing both fractures the Conclave, which may produce Mirror-endings where the party alone determines the outcome. Every faction sees the Thing differently, and their truths are all partially correct.

sideQuests.title: The Outcast’s Plea
sideQuests.description: A banished mutant seer begs the party to retrieve a memory crystal lost in the conclave's depths, promising visions of the future in return. The crystal contains a different prophecy per playline: the dreamer's next cycle, the containment seal's next failure, the next communion window, the next ancestral awakening, or the next reflection the mirror will show. Which future the seer offers depends on which truth the party has been living.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Provides prophetic warnings or clues for the final battle.

sideQuests.title: Seeds of Dissent
sideQuests.description: The players discover a faction within the conclave that secretly opposes the ancient consciousness. They are sleepers who wish to keep dreaming, wardens who maintain containment from within, gradualists who prefer slow communion, separators who resist ancestral reversion, or reflectors who believe fear should be studied not served. The party can choose to ally with these dissenters or expose them for a reward.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Potential reinforcements or sabotage in climax, or extra rewards.

plotPoints.title: Confronting the Source
plotPoints.description: The party descends into the pulsing heart of the Aberrant Wastes, where the ancient consciousness--an alien entity merged with the land--awaits. The Heartstone ritual chamber reveals the final truth about what the presence below truly is, but the ritual itself means different things per playline: a mood-stabilizer for a dreaming god, an anchor-sacrifice to reinforce containment, a communion-accelerator to complete the joining, a reversion-catalyst to restore ancestral form, or a fear-focus that concentrates terror into a weapon. This confrontation, blending combat, psychic challenges, and environmental hazards, directly shapes the fate of the region and which playline dominates the ending.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Using the Heartstone as stabilizer pushes toward Dreamer or Containment endings. Using it as accelerator favors Communion or Inheritance. Skipping the ritual leaves all playlines open but weakens the party's influence on the final outcome. The presence responds differently to each choice, revealing which interpretation it has been wearing all along--or whether it has been wearing all of them at once.

sideQuests.title: Shatter the Heartstone
sideQuests.description: A risky ritual can be attempted to weaken the alien consciousness, but it requires rare reagents and leaves participants vulnerable. The Heartstone at the ritual's center may function as a dream-suppressant, a sacrifice to reinforce containment, a communion-accelerator, a reversion-catalyst, or a fear-focus depending on the ritual's alignment. The reagents themselves shift meaning: dream-herbs, containment-crystals, communion-nectar, ancestral-bone, or mirror-shard.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Reduces final boss’s power, but imposes conditions/exhaustion on the party.

plotPoints.title: Into the Heart of the Shuddering Wilds
plotPoints.description: With the source of the corruption disrupted or contained, the party is drawn to the Shuddering Wilds (TTL001)--the forest above the Ancients Lab. Here, unnatural mists and tremors grow stronger, and the land itself seems to breathe with something vast beneath it. The mists may be the exhalation of a dreaming god, the leakage of a failing containment seal, the call of a lonely intelligence seeking communion, the ancestral memory of what this place once was, or the reflected fears of every living thing that has entered. The party must navigate treacherous paths and decipher signs of something colossal stirring deep underground, seeking a way to reach the sealed laboratory at the wilds' core.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Establishes the Wilds' menacing tone and introduces the five-playline atmospheric framework that will intensify as the party approaches the Lab. Every environmental detail the party notices may be a clue about which truth the land carries.

sideQuests.title: Echoes in the Fog
sideQuests.description: A series of echoing, mournful cries lead the party to a lost herbalist's camp. The cries may be dream-echoes from the sleeper's mind, containment-breach alarms, communion-attempts from the presence below, ancestral laments, or the party's own fears given voice. Rescuing the herbalist from carnivorous plants could provide useful knowledge and a strange herbal concoction that functions differently per playline.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Herbalist’s aid can grant advantage on certain saves or skills in the Wilds.

sideQuests.title: Watcher in the Thicket
sideQuests.description: The party notices they are being observed by a mysterious, masked figure who vanishes into the mist. The figure may be a dream-walker from the sleeper's subconscious, a containment-scout checking for unauthorized entry, a communion-herald evaluating candidates, an ancestral wraith recognizing kin, or the party's own collective fear observing itself. Following them leads to a cache of old maps and warnings scrawled in an ancient dialect that reads differently depending on the reader's dominant playline.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Old maps may reveal hidden paths or dangers, aiding future navigation.

plotPoints.title: Whispers Beneath the Canopy
plotPoints.description: Delving deeper into the Shuddering Wilds, the party observes increasingly unnatural phenomena and learns that the land is warped by the ancient laboratory below. To reach the lab, they must seek out the enigmatic Speaker of the Mists, whose riddles are the key to breaching the wards protecting the entrance. The Speaker appears differently to each observer: a dream-speaker who recites prophecies from the sleeper's mind, a ward-sentinel who tests whether visitors carry containment protocols, a communion-herald who offers the joining, an ancestral voice that speaks in genealogical riddles, or a reflection of the party's own deepest questions given form and voice.
plotPoints.plotImpact: The Speaker's riddles contain different keys depending on which interpretation the party has been leaning toward. Solving via dream-logic opens the Dreamer path; via protocol opens Containment; via acceptance opens Communion; via genealogy opens Inheritance; via self-knowledge opens the Mirror. The party may not realize they are choosing their ending family with each answer.

sideQuests.title: The Corrupted Grove
sideQuests.description: A section of forest is dying, blighted by toxic ooze from below. The blight manifests as dream-decay where the sleeper's nightmares bleed through, containment-leakage where the seal erodes, communion-overload where the joining is too much too fast, ancestral-reversion where the land reverts to an older state, or fear-corruption where reflected terror poisons the soil. Purging the corruption (by fighting or negotiating with warped fey) earns the gratitude of the forest's lesser spirits.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Spirits grant boons (temporary benefits or a clue for negotiating with the Speaker of the Mists).

sideQuests.title: Moss-Covered Relics
sideQuests.description: Adventurers find relics partially unearthed by the tremors--remnants of ancient technology. The relics respond differently to each approach: as dream-tuning instruments, containment-calibration tools, communion-interface devices, ancestry-attuned mechanisms, or mirror-framing lenses. Restoring or understanding these devices could help communicate with the Speaker of the Mists by speaking the language of whichever truth the relic embodies.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Successful identification provides leverage in social or arcane challenges.

plotPoints.title: Revelations at the Sunken Threshold
plotPoints.description: Guided by the Speaker's riddles, the party locates the sunken entrance to the Ancients Lab. The colossal presence beneath the Wilds begins to awaken, causing dangerous tremors and unleashing mutated guardians. The entrance is protected by a ward circle that functions differently per playline: a dream-gate that regulates the sleeper's breath, a containment-seal that holds shut the door, a communion-door that opens only for the willing, an ancestry-ward that responds to blood, or a fear-cage that imprisons terror itself. The party must solve the entrance puzzle and decide whether to repair the ward circle, disrupt it, or pass through it entirely.
plotPoints.plotImpact: Repairing the ward strengthens whichever playline the ward currently serves (Dreamer-soothing or Containment-reinforcement). Disrupting it opens the path for Communion or Inheritance. Entering through the ward by satisfying its condition (dreaming, containment-protocol, communion-acceptance, ancestral-recognition, or facing fear) commits the party to that playline for the finale. Each variant changes the guardians, the lab's interior, and the Thing's opening stance.

sideQuests.title: The Broken Circle
sideQuests.description: A broken magical ward circle at the entrance could be repaired or disrupted. The circle is a dream-gate regulating the sleeper's breath, a containment-seal holding shut the door, a communion-door that opens only for the willing, an ancestry-ward that responds to blood, or a fear-cage that imprisons terror itself. Repairing it may hold off the awakening force temporarily but requires rare reagents from the Wilds; disrupting it could grant boons to the party but hasten the emergence of the thing below. Which function the circle serves determines the consequences of either choice.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Player choice here alters the tempo of the adventure and the type of final encounter.

plotPoints.title: The Heart Beneath the Wilds
plotPoints.description: The party descends into the Ancients Lab (TTL001), now aware that their every move resonates with the stirring behemoth below. This is the convergence point where all five truths meet. Grahl reveals their full per-playline truth; Hesk faces their full per-playline dilemma. The Prototype Cure may be a dream-suppressant, a sacrifice of self to reinforce the seal, a communion-reversal serum, a reversion-pause for ancestral transformation, or a fear-release that dissolves the Mirror. The Rune-etched Collar functions as a dream-tether, a containment-anchor, a communion-link, an ancestry-key, or a fear-magnifier depending on which playline dominates. The Narrator SHALL select the ending family based on which playline received the most emergence triggers during gameplay. The 15 possible endings are: DREAMER (A1: The Dreamer Returns to Sleep, A2: The Dreamer Wakens, A3: You Become the Dream); CONTAINMENT (B1: The Warden Endures, B2: The Seal Breaks, B3: You Become the New Warden); COMMUNION (C1: Communion Completed, C2: Communion Rejected, C3: Partial Communion); INHERITANCE (D1: The Cycle Continues, D2: The Reversion Completes, D3: A New Separation); MIRROR (E1: The Mirror Shatters, E2: The Mirror Holds, E3: You Become the Mirror).
plotPoints.plotImpact: The final ending is determined by playline dominance: count emergence triggers from PP004 (ward choice), PP007 (reality choice), PP008 (faction choice), PP009 (Heartstone choice), and PP012 (ward circle choice). The dominant playline selects the ending family; the specific variant (1/2/3) depends on degree of commitment, party cohesion, and whether the party sought to control, accept, or transcend the truth. If two playlines are tied, the party must make a final explicit choice. The ending reshapes the Shuddering Wilds and determines the fate of every NPC who survived the journey.

sideQuests.title: The Last Attendant
sideQuests.description: A surviving, semi-sapient construct within the lab claims to serve the Ancients. It offers aid--or betrayal--depending on how the party treats it and what they promise about the future of the Wilds. Its service manifests per playline: lullaby-singer for the Dreamer, protocol-enforcer for Containment, welcome-host for Communion, genealogist for Inheritance, or truth-teller for the Mirror. It remembers every version of the truth and may reveal whichever one the party has earned.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Can provide critical support in the final confrontation or sabotage the party depending on their choices.

sideQuests.title: Echoes of the Past
sideQuests.description: Fragments of ancient logs offer glimpses into what the Ancients tried and failed to accomplish. The logs contain five parallel accounts: researchers trying to soothe a dreamer, wardens struggling to maintain containment, seekers attempting communion, genealogists tracing ancestral lineage, and mirror-engineers building a reflection chamber. Piecing these together may reveal hidden weaknesses or bargaining chips against the thing below--or reveal that all five experiments were the same experiment seen through different eyes.
sideQuests.plotImpact: Aids the party in the final encounter or offers insight into the larger campaign’s mysteries.

sideQuests.title: The Archivist’s Bargain
sideQuests.description: An ancient archivist automaton offers a deal: preserve its records in exchange for knowledge or aid in subduing the Thing. Hesk's records contain every truth the facility has ever told, but it can only show, never state. The party must decide whether to trust this relic of the past--and whether the records it preserves are dream-archives, containment-logs, communion-testimonies, genealogical-records, or mirror-captures. The answer may be all of them simultaneously.
sideQuests.plotImpact: May offer magical or tactical assistance, or create new complications if betrayed.
